# [2404.08191] Measuring Cross-lingual Transfer in Bytes

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.08191) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08191v1)
> Abstract:Multilingual pretraining has been a successful solution to the challenges posed by the lack of resources for languages. These models can transfer knowledge to target languages with minimal or no examples. Recent research suggests that monolingual models also have a similar capability, but the mechanisms behind this transfer remain unclear. Some studies have explored factors like language contamination and syntactic similarity. An emerging line of research suggests that the representations learned by language models contain two components: a language-specific and a language-agnostic component. The latter is responsible for transferring a more universal knowledge. However, there is a lack of comprehensive exploration of these properties across diverse target languages. To investigate this hypothesis, we conducted an experiment inspired by the work on the Scaling Laws for Transfer. We measured the amount of data transferred from a source language to a target language and found that models initialized from diverse languages perform similarly to a target language in a cross-lingual setting. This was surprising because the amount of data transferred to 10 diverse target languages, such as Spanish, Korean, and Finnish, was quite similar. We also found evidence that this transfer is not related to language contamination or language proximity, which strengthens the hypothesis that the model also relies on language-agnostic knowledge. Our experiments have opened up new possibilities for measuring how much data represents the language-agnostic representations learned during pretraining.

## Submission history

Leandro Rodrigues de Souza

FEEC, UNICAMP, Brazil

Abstract

Multilingual pretraining has been a successful  
solution to the challenges posed by the lack  
of resources for languages. These models can  
transfer knowledge to target languages with  
minimal or no examples. Recent research sug-  
gests that monolingual models also have a sim-  
ilar capability, but the mechanisms behind this  
transfer remain unclear. Some studies have ex-  
plored factors like language contamination and  
syntactic similarity. An emerging line of re-  
search suggests that the representations learned  
by language models contain two components:  
a language-specific and a language-agnostic  
component. The latter is responsible for trans-  
ferring a more universal knowledge. However,  
there is a lack of comprehensive exploration of  
these properties across diverse target languages.

To investigate this hypothesis, we conducted an

experiment inspired by the work on the Scaling  
Laws for Transfer. We measured the amount  
of data transferred from a source language to a  
target language and found that models initial-  
ized from diverse languages perform similarly  
to a target language in a cross-lingual setting.

This was surprising because the amount of data

transferred to 10 diverse target languages, such  
as Spanish, Korean, and Finnish, was quite sim-  
ilar. We also found evidence that this trans-  
fer is not related to language contamination or  
language proximity, which strengthens the hy-  
pothesis that the model also relies on language-  
agnostic knowledge. Our experiments have  
opened up new possibilities for measuring how  
much data represents the language-agnostic rep-  
resentations learned during [pretraining.1](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#1)

1

Introduction

The emergence of self-supervised pretraining mod-

els such as BERT has revealed a notable phe-  
nomenon of cross-lingual transfer even when these

LLAMA [(Touvron et al., 2023), ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)which was trained  
self-supervisedly on an English-centric corpus, ex-  
hibits surprising multilingual capabilities [(Yuan et al., 2023; Ye et al., 2023). ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)The underlying mech-  
anisms driving this behavior remain unclear, with  
hypotheses ranging from the presence of shared

“anchor” tokens [(Pires et al., 2019) ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)to language con-

tamination [(Blevins and Zettlemoyer, 2022), ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)yet no  
scientific consensus has been reached.

Research in this area often involves the use of

pre-existing language models (LMs), which are  
subsequently finetuned on supervised datasets in  
different languages [(de Souza et al., 2021; ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)[Yuan et al., 2023). ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)However, when evaluating multiple  
languages, conventional methodologies encounter  
two significant challenges: firstly, the dependence  
on supervised finetuning datasets, which often vary  
in size and quality, complicating cross-lingual com-  
parisons; secondly, the use of subword tokenizers,

which do not represent all languages equally.

In this work, we avoid these problems by work-

ing with a byte-level tokenizer and by using  
auto-regressive language models trained in self-  
supervised from scratch in one language and then  
finetuned on another. To measure the effect of  
transfer learning, we employ the concept of data  
transfer [(Hernandez et al., 2021), ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)which allows us  
to quantify how much each different source lan-  
guage contributes to the perplexity of the target  
language.

Our main contribution is providing a method that

measures how much knowledge, in bytes, is trans-  
ferred from one language to another. By applying  
it, our findings reveal a surprising trend: even when  
comparing linguistically distant languages, the data  
transfer metrics are of a comparable magnitude.

This research contributes additional evidence sup-

porting the language-agnostic hypothesis, which  
suggests that the internal representations developed

2

Related Work

Prior work attributed the success of multilingual  
models in cross-lingual transfer to “anchor” to-  
kens [(Pires et al., 2019). ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)However, subsequent  
research demonstrated that models could perform

well even without these tokens [(Artetxe et al.,](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)

[2020), ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)highlighting the significance of shared pa-  
rameters during training [(Conneau et al., 2020). ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)Competitive results were achieved by monolingual  
models with minimal or no adaptation [(Artetxe et al., 2020; de Souza et al., 2021).](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)

Investigations by [Blevins and Zettlemoyer](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)

[(2022) ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)linked these findings to language contami-

nation, where pretraining datasets contained target  
language data. Additional factors contributing to  
cross-lingual transfer success include dataset statis-  
tics, language attributes [(Lin et al., 2019), ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)language  
structure [(Lin et al., 2019; Papadimitriou and Ju- rafsky, 2020; Chiang and yi Lee, 2020; Ri and](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)

[Tsuruoka, 2022), ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)and token overlap between train-

ing and target languages [(Beukman and Fokam, 2023). ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)The role of language script [(Fujinuma et al., 2022) ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)and model tokenizer [(Rust et al., 2021) ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)was  
also noted, prompting the use of a byte tokenizer  
to address these issues [(Xue et al., 2022; ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)[Abonizio et al., 2022).](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)

Recent research proposed a two-component

model representation hypothesis—language agnos-  
tic and language specific [(de Souza et al., 2021; ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)[Zeng et al., 2023; Wu et al., 2022). ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)While promis-  
ing, no study has measured how much of the  
language-agnostic component is used in settings

with multiple source and target languages. Addi-

tionally, existing research still applies the source  
language vocabulary to the target language, po-  
tentially compromising input representations and  
affecting results.

To address these gaps, we draw on [Hernandez](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)

[et al. (2021) ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)and employ a byte vocabulary in our  
experiments to overcome current literature limita-  
tions.

3

Methodology

Inspired by [Hernandez et al. (2021), ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)our method-  
ology focuses on quantifying the transferability of  
pretraining data across distributions, particularly  
between different languages. We select a target

language and finetune models initialized from var-  
ious source languages onto it. Subsequently, we  
evaluate each model on a target language test set  
and compare their performance. We introduce the  
Data Transfer (DT ) metric to estimate knowledge  
transfer, explained in more depth in [3.1\. ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#2)This pro-  
cess is repeated across different target languages to  
observe effects across a broad linguistic spectrum.

These experiments aim to quantify and compare

cross-lingual knowledge transfer from different  
source languages. This analysis seeks to uncover  
the extent to which transferability depends on spe-  
cific languages and the importance of language-  
agnostic components in learned representations.

The following sections provide further details.

3.1

Data Transfer Estimation

To quantify the knowledge transfer from pretrained

models to a given target language, we utilize the  
Data Transfer (DT ) metric. This metric assesses  
the effectiveness of pretraining data by measuring  
the additional tokens required in the target language  
for a model initialized from scratch to match the  
performance of a model pretrained on a source  
language and finetuned on the target. Figure [1 ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#3)illustrates this concept.

In our experiments, we utilize a set of

M different dataset sizes, denoted as DF =  
{s0, s1, ..., sm}, in the target language. Initially,

we train a random-initialized model on these

datasets, resulting in a set of perplexities PR =  
{pr,0, pr,1, ..., pr,m}. Subsequently, we train from  
scratch another model on a fixed amount of tokens

(e.g., 6B) in a source language ℓ, and then finetune

it on the target language using the same dataset  
sizes DF, generating another set of perplexities  
Pℓ = {pℓ,0, pℓ,1, ..., pℓ,m}.

To estimate the Data Effective metric (DE),

which represents the amount of data needed to

achieve a certain performance, we utilize a linear  
interpolation function γ(y′, X, Y). This function  
interpolates between discrete data points (xj, yj) ∈  
X × Y , evaluated at y′. In our case, the calculation  
is expressed as:

DE,i = γ(pℓ,i, DF, PR)

(1)

Here, DE,i signifies the Data Effective metric

for the i-th perplexity value in Pℓ. PR denotes the  
set of perplexity values derived from the random-  
initialized model, while DF represents the dataset  
sizes employed during finetuning.

3.2

Task and Evaluation Metric

We adopt Language Modeling as our main task  
with perplexity as the performance metric for

all experiments.

Perplexity, derived from the

model’s loss (eloss), facilitates future predictions of  
model behavior in transfer learning scenarios, fol-  
lowing the approach in [Hernandez et al. (2021).](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)

This choice also allows extensive experiments

across multiple languages, leveraging datasets like  
mC4 [(Xue et al., 2021) ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)to overcome size limitations  
inherent in supervised datasets.

3.3

Tokenization Impact

In cross-lingual setups, the choice of tokenization  
method holds considerable significance [(Rust et al., 2021). ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)While subword tokenizers are commonly

employed in cross-lingual experiments, using a to-  
kenizer trained in a source language on a distant  
target language may result in an increased number  
of tokens. This can lead to the utilization of un-  
dertrained embeddings in some instances, introduc-  
ing challenges for effective sentence representation.  
Furthermore, dealing with different scripts intro-  
duces the issue of numerous “unknown” tokens,  
exacerbating the difficulty of obtaining suitable in-  
put representations for the model.

To address these challenges, we opt for a byte

vocabulary based on the approach proposed by  
[Xue et al. (2022), ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)which allows us to standardize

representations across all languages, ensuring that  
each model encounters the same quantity of UTF-8  
bytes. By doing so, we mitigate the use of unknown  
tokens and undertrained embeddings, thereby min-  
imizing the impact of tokenization issues on the  
performance of our experiments.

3.4

Language Contamination

A potential reason for a pretrained model’s supe-

rior performance in cross-lingual tasks is the pres-  
ence of a substantial amount of data in the target  
language in its pretraining dataset, a phenomenon  
referred to as language contamination. To quan-  
tify this impact, following the approach outlined  
by [Blevins and Zettlemoyer (2022), ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)we examine  
the rates of target language fragments in the source  
language dataset and vice versa.

Specifically, for a given source language ℓ and

target language t, we calculate the ratio of all lines

classified as ℓ in the target dataset (known as con-  
tamination on target) and as t in the pretraining  
dataset (known as contamination on source). We

Correlating these rates with the model’s data

3.5

Language Similarity

Language similarity is often cited as a crucial fac-  
tor influencing cross-lingual transfer performance  
in natural language processing tasks. In this work,

we aim to investigate the relationship between lan-

guage similarity and cross-lingual transfer effec-  
tiveness based on the outcomes of our experiments.

To explore this relationship, we measure various

distances between languages, including syntactic,  
geographic, and phonological distances. These  
distances are calculated based on the methodology  
proposed by [Littell et al. (2017).](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)

We aim to correlate these language distances

with the data transfer metric (DT ). By employing

Spearman correlation analysis, we seek to discern

whether there exists a significant correlation be-

tween the observed DT values and the measured  
language distances.

This analysis elucidates whether our experimen-

tal results can be attributed to the similarities be-  
tween the languages involved in our cross-lingual  
experiments.

4

Experiments

This section presents the languages, datasets,

model architecture, and training details for our ex-  
periments.

4.1

Languages

diverse languages—English, Russian, and Chi-  
nese—for the source language during the pretrain-  
ing phase. This selection ensures a broad linguistic  
spectrum while adhering to pretraining budget con-  
straints.

4.2

Datasets

For training and finetuning, language subsets from  
the mC4 dataset [(Xue et al., 2021) ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)for the selected  
languages were utiliz[ed.3 ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#4)Pretraining datasets com-  
prised approximately 6 billion tokens, while fine-  
tuning datasets ranged from 6 million to 6 billion  
tokens. Documents were sampled at random with-  
out replacement until the desired amount of tokens

was reached.

4.3

Model Architecture

Our model is a decoder-only Transformer [(Vaswani et al., 2017) ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)that uses a byte vocabulary with 256  
embeddings with a dimension of 640\. The model  
follows closely the implementation provided in  
the T5x library. It consists of 10 layers, each  
having 10 attention heads with dimensions of 64.

The intermediate dimension of Multi-Layer Percep-

tron (MLP) has a dimension of 2560 and GELU

[(Hendrycks and Gimpel, 2023) ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)activations. The

parameters of the embeddings matrix and the final  
dense layer are shared. We use relative positional  
embeddings [(Shaw et al., 2018). ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)The resulting  
model has approximately 65 million parameters.

4.4

Training details

Models were trained using a causal language mod-  
eling objective. Each batch has 512 sequences of

1024 tokens. We use the AdamW optimizer with an

initial learning rate of 2e-4, which decayed to 2e-  
5 through cosine decay following [Hoffmann et al.](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)

[(2022). ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)Finetuning employed a constant learning

rate of 2e-5 over 10 epochs, except for the 6 bil-  
lion dataset size where we limited it to 3 epochs.

A clear pattern emerges: one initialization stands

tered results are observed for Arabic (ar), German

With three diverse initializations, the fact that

two consistently show similar DT values, even

when distant from the target language (e.g., Russian

and Chinese for Finnish), suggests the models lever-  
age language-agnostic representations. This obser-

vation aligns with the expected behavior, where

DT would be close to zero if language-specific  
knowledge were dominant.

English (en) demonstrates effective knowledge

transfer to most target languages, potentially due  
to its widespread presence in corpora across lan-  
guages. This hypothesis is explored further in Sec-

transfer effectively to Japanese (ja) and Korean

(ko), likely due to their linguistic proximity.

We observe that Chinese (zh) tends to transfer

effectively to Japanese (ja) and Korean (ko), both  
of which are considered closer languages. This,  
together with our other observations, indicates that,

while not determinant, language-specific compo-

6

Discussion

Our study aims to measure how much knowledge,  
in bytes, is transferred from one language to an-  
other, enabling the investigation of the effective-  
ness of language-agnostic representations acquired  
during pretraining in cross-lingual scenarios. We  
hypothesize that these representations enable mod-  
els to perform well on downstream tasks across  
diverse languages, which is observed in state-of-  
the-art multilingual models.

In our results, we consistently find that at least

two source languages demonstrate very close DT

values when evaluated against a target language,

despite the diverse set of script systems and lin-  
guistic characteristics involved. This observation  
suggests that the data transferred from these lan-  
guages to the target language is not primarily re-  
lated to language-specific components but rather  
to language-agnostic ones. For instance, as illus-  
trated in Figure [3, ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#6)both English and Russian, de-  
spite being known as distant languages, achieve  
nearly identical DT values when evaluated on Ko-  
rean, a language distinct from either. Moreover, all  
three source languages are remarkably close when  
evaluated on the Japanese test set.

Despite exposure to only a few tokens in the

target language, our models demonstrate similar  
perplexity performance, indicating high adaptabil-  
ity and generalization across a broad range of  
languages.

This reinforces the notion that the

language-agnostic component plays a crucial, uni-  
form role across source languages.

Notably, our results are not attributed to pre-

training exposure to target languages, since there  
is a weak correlation of language contamination

with the data transfer coefficient. Additionally, the

observed performance is not solely dependent on  
language proximity, as suggested in other works.

While perplexity offers valuable insights, gener-

alizable conclusions require evaluation in down-  
stream tasks, especially in under-resourced lan-  
guages. To explore this further, we conducted a  
small-scale experiment, detailed in Appendix [A, ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)finetuning our pretrained models for a low-resource  
language inference task. Surprisingly, we observe  
comparable accuracy scores between Portuguese  
and Russian, with good results also for English

 link to page 10 link to page 10 link to page 11 link to page 11 link to page 10 link to page 10 

and Chinese, suggesting that our initial findings

with perplexity may extend broadly. However, a

more detailed investigation is required to under-  
stand cross-lingual transfer mechanisms fully.

The novelty of our approach is employing a

byte-level tokenizer and adapting [Hernandez et al.](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)

[(2021) ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)for a cross-lingual scenario.

The byte-

level approach facilitates consistent model em-  
beddings across diverse scripts, enabling effective  
cross-lingual knowledge transfer without language-  
specific tokenization or preprocessing. This is sup-  
ported by the strong performance of ByT5 com-  
pared to mT5 in [Xue et al. (2022).](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)

In conclusion, our study suggests the presence of

language-agnostic representations contributing to  
cross-lingual transferability, while also laying the  
foundation to measure it through the Data Transfer  
metric. The observed consistency in model per-  
formance across diverse languages, facilitated by  
the byte-level tokenizer, indicates the potential for  
more efficient and generalizable natural language  
understanding across linguistic boundaries in com-  
putational linguistics and NLP.

7

Limitations

Our study has certain limitations that merit consid-  
eration. Firstly, our choice of initializing models

with only three languages, while diverse, leaves

room for improvement. Including additional lan-  
guages in the pretraining phase would enhance the  
robustness of our analysis by minimizing possi-  
ble bias towards the selected languages while pro-

viding more samples for our correlation analysis.

However, this expansion would necessitate a more  
substantial computational budget.

Secondly, our reliance on small models, specifi-

cally a 65 million parameter model, limits the scope  
of our findings as larger models may exhibit dif-  
ferent behavior. Additionally, the capacity of very  
large models for few-shot learning opens avenues  
for further exploration in the domain of transfer  
learning.

Lastly, the heterogeneity of the mC4 dataset

across languages introduces a potential source of

variability in the models’ exposure to different

knowledge. While the impact of this variation on  
data transfer remains unclear, conducting experi-  
ments with controlled datasets would offer valuable  
insights. Moreover, employing a more compara-  
ble test set could help mitigate statistical variance,  
particularly in analyses such as the commutative

property assessment.

8

Conclusion and Future Work

Our study delves into the transferability of knowl-  
edge in cross-lingual scenarios, leveraging a byte-  
level tokenizer and an adapted methodology in-  
spired by [Hernandez et al. (2021). ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)By measuring  
the models’ reliance on pretraining when execut-  
ing tasks in diverse languages, our approach offers  
an understanding of the cross-lingual capabilities  
of language models. The results provide evidence  
that language-agnostic representations also play  
an important role in downstream tasks. This not  
only contributes to the current understanding of  
cross-lingual transferability but also serves as a cat-  
alyst for further exploration into the properties of  
language-agnostic knowledge transfer. For future  
research directions, we envision key investigations  
that can build upon the insights presented in this  
paper:

1\. Expand Experiment Range:

Use more

source languages so we can draw stronger con-  
clusions.

2\. Controlled Datasets Usage: Employ con-

trolled datasets and comparable test sets to  
address mC4 dataset heterogeneity, offering  
clearer insights into varied knowledge expo-  
sure impact on cross-lingual transferability  
and mitigating variance.

3\. Explore Larger Models: Investigate the use

of larger models in few-shot learning down-  
stream tasks as complementary evaluations to  
perplexity measurements.

4\. Measure DT from Non-natural languages:

Perform experiments with non-natural lan-  
guage data, such as artificial languages with  
hierarchical structures. This exploration could  
shed light on whether knowledge transfer pri-  
marily occurs due to the content of pretraining  
or is largely influenced by the linguistic form.

A

Appendix: Downstream Task  
Experiment

To further explore the generalizability of our find-

ings beyond casual language modeling with the  
perplexity metric, we conducted an additional ex-  
periment focusing on a distinct downstream task.

This experiment involved finetuning our models

pretrained on the selected source languages for a  
specific downstream task, targeting a different lan-  
guage.

A.1

Experiment Details

For this experiment, we selected Portuguese as the  
target language and the Recognizing Textual En-  
tailment (RTE) task from the ASSIN2 [(Real et al., 2020)](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#10)[5 ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#11)dataset. The dataset comprised 6,500 train-  
ing examples and 500 validation instances.

We finetuned the source models for 10 epochs

using a constant learning rate of 5e − 5 and a batch  
size of 128\. The objective of the task was to predict

whether one sentence entails another, with evalua-

tion based on accuracy measured on the validation  
set.

A.2

Results

Our results, summarized in Table [7, ](1793563298553-5750571c-aae7-4121-982c-8067b6ff8e26-file65884.html#12)reveal compa-  
rable performance between Portuguese (our base-  
line) and Russian, despite being considered a dis-  
tant language. English lags by nearly 6 percentage  
points compared to our baseline, while Chinese ex-  
hibits the poorest performance, trailing our baseline  
by almost 20 percentage points.

Despite the limited scope of our experiment,

focusing on only one target language and task,  
these findings suggest significant knowledge trans-  
fer across languages with varying degrees of sim-  
ilarity. For example, even with the lowest perfor-  
mance observed in Chinese, it still outperforms a

Based on our findings, cross-lingual knowledge

transfer appears to occur even with more distant lan-  
guages. These results underscore the importance of  
further exploration in this area, indicating a promis-  
ing potential for measuring knowledge transfer in  
cross-lingual scenarios and delineating the contri-  
butions of language-agnostic and language-specific

# [2410.12049] Sabiá-3 Technical Report

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.12049) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v4)
> Abstract:This report presents Sabiá-3, our new flagship language model, and Sabiazinho-3, a more cost-effective sibling. The models were trained on a large brazilian-centric corpus. Evaluations across diverse professional and academic benchmarks show a strong performance on Portuguese and Brazil-related tasks. Sabiá-3 shows large improvements in comparison to our previous best of model, Sabia-2 Medium, especially in reasoning-intensive tasks. Notably, Sabiá-3's average performance matches frontier LLMs, while it is offered at a three to four times lower cost per token, reinforcing the benefits of domain specialization.

# [2410.12049v4] Sabiá-3 Technical Report

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.12049v4) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v4)
> Abstract:This report presents Sabiá-3, our new flagship language model, and Sabiazinho-3, a more cost-effective sibling. The models were trained on a large brazilian-centric corpus. Evaluations across diverse professional and academic benchmarks show a strong performance on Portuguese and Brazil-related tasks. Sabiá-3 shows large improvements in comparison to our previous best of model, Sabia-2 Medium, especially in reasoning-intensive tasks. Notably, Sabiá-3's average performance matches frontier LLMs, while it is offered at a three to four times lower cost per token, reinforcing the benefits of domain specialization.

Portanto, a referência correta para o cenário atual e futuro imediato é o **Ranking 2025**.

## World University Rankings 2025

You are viewing a past edition of our rankings.

Explore the *Times Higher Education* World University Rankings 2025 below. Trusted worldwide by students, teachers, governments and industry experts, the list ranks 2,092 institutions from 115 countries and territories.

## University rankings 2025: highlights

- Oxford holds on to the top spot for the ninth consecutive year, bolstered by significant improvements in industry engagement and teaching
- MIT rises to second place, overtaking Stanford, which drops to sixth
- China edges closer to the top 10, further boosting its global research influence
- Australia’s top five universities all slip down the rankings, due to declining reputation and international outlook
- Three new countries join the top 200 - Brazil, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates - highlighting the rise of emerging markets in higher education

For broader coverage of this topic, see [Universities and Higher Education in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universities_and_Higher_Education_in_Brazil "Universities and Higher Education in Brazil").

Universities in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") are ranked in a number of ways, including both national and international ranks.

## National Rankings

### Ranking Universitário Folha

### Brazilian government evaluation

Higher education evaluations are also conducted by the Brazilian Government; specifically by **Inep** (Instituto Nacional de Estudos e
Pesquisas Educacionais; English: National Institute of Studies and Research). The Government uses a **General Index of Courses** (Portuguese: [Índice Geral de Cursos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice_Geral_de_Cursos?action=edit&redlink=1 "Índice Geral de Cursos (page does not exist)") [[pt](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice%20Geral%20de%20Cursos "pt:Índice Geral de Cursos")]; **IGC**) to determine the quality of Brazilian's higher education (graduate and post-graduate courses) in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"). [Universidade de São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidade_de_São_Paulo "Universidade de São Paulo"), one of the most prestigious universities in the country, has been participating in the **IGC** since 2013 as part of a technical cooperation with **Inep** that will last three years, during which time the results concerning the university's courses will not be disclosed. Only then will the university decide whether to fully participate in the government evaluation.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rankings_of_universities_in_Brazil#cite_note-RUF-1)

resposta:
Aqui está a lista dos ministros brasileiros da Agricultura (Ministério da Agricultura, Pecuária e Abastecimento - MAPA) desde o início de 2018 até o fim de 2024:

*   **Tereza Cristina**
    *   **Período:** 1º de janeiro de 2019 a 30 de março de 2022.
    *   **Presidente:** Jair Bolsonaro.
    *   *Nota:* Não houve ministro entre o início de 2018 e o início de 2019, pois o cargo estava vago ou em transição até a posse de Tereza Cristina em janeiro de 2019.

*   **Marcos Montes**
    *   **Período:** 30 de março de 2022 a 31 de dezembro de 2022.
    *   **Presidente:** Jair Bolsonaro.

*   **Carlos Fávaro**
    *   **Período:** 1º de janeiro de 2023 a 31 de março de 2026 (atualmente).
    *   **Presidente:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
    *   *Nota:* O mandato de Carlos Fávaro foi prorrogado para 2026 após o primeiro mandato original (2023-2024). Portanto, ele também ministrou durante todo o ano de 2024.

# Lista de ministros da Agricultura e Pecuária do Brasil

Esta é uma **lista de [ministros da Agricultura e Pecuária](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministério_da_Agricultura_e_Pecuária "Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária")** do [Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil "Brasil").[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Agricultura_e_Pecu%C3%A1ria_do_Brasil#cite_note-ministerio-1)

Até 1892, com a denominação de Secretaria de Estado dos Negócios da Agricultura, Comércio e Obras Públicas, tinha responsabilidades tanto sobre a [agricultura](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultura "Agricultura") quanto o [transporte](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transporte "Transporte"), por isso a [lista de Ministros dos Transportes do Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_dos_Transportes_do_Brasil "Lista de ministros dos Transportes do Brasil") repete o nome dos ministros da Agricultura até 1892.[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Agricultura_e_Pecu%C3%A1ria_do_Brasil#cite_note-ministerio-1)

# [2308.11878] Cabrita: closing the gap for foreign languages

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.11878) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2308.11878v1)
> Abstract:The strategy of training the model from scratch in a specific language or domain serves two essential purposes: i) enhancing performance in the particular linguistic or domain context, and ii) ensuring effective tokenization. The main limitation inherent to this approach lies in the associated cost, which can reach six to seven-digit dollar values, depending on the model size and the number of parameters involved.
>
> The main solution to overcome the cost challenge is to rely on available pre-trained models, which, despite recent advancements such as the LLaMA and LLaMA-2 models, still demonstrate inefficiency for certain specific domain problems or prove ineffective in scenarios involving conversational memory resources, given the large number of tokens required to represent text.
> To overcome this issue, we present a methodology named Cabrita, which, as our research demonstrates, successfully addresses the performance and efficient tokenization problem, all at an affordable cost. We believe that this methodology can be applied to any transformer-like architecture model. To validate the study, we conducted continuous pre-training exclusively using Portuguese text on a 3-billion-parameter model known as OpenLLaMA, resulting in a model named openCabrita 3B. The openCabrita 3B also features a new tokenizer that results in a significant reduction in the number of tokens required to represent the text. In our assessment, for few-shot learning tasks, we achieved similar results with this 3B model compared to a traditional continuous pre-training approach as well as to 7B models English pre-trained models.

## Submission history

pergunta: Can you make a report about all the Nightlord bosses of elden ring Nightreign. I also want know all the unique relics dropped by defeating each nightlord for the first time. I also want to know the main elemental weakness of each nightlord.
resposta:
Here is a comprehensive report on the **Nightlord bosses** in *Elden Ring: Nightreign*, including their unique relics, elemental weaknesses, and key characteristics.

### **Overview**
In *Elden Ring: Nightreign*, players face powerful "Nightlords" at the end of the third day (Night 3) of an Expedition. Unlike standard Night Bosses, which are randomized, the final Nightlord is selected by the player via the **Table of Lost Grace** at the Roundtable Hold. There are **8 primary Nightlords** available in the base game, plus **2 DLC Nightlords** from *The Forsaken Hollows*.

---

### **1. Gladius, Beast of Night (Tricephalos)**
*   **Description:** A massive three-headed demonic wolf wielding a chained greatsword. It can split into three separate one-headed wolves.
*   **Primary Weakness:** **Holy Damage**. (Also vulnerable to Critical Attacks after stance break).
*   **Unique Relic Dropped (First Victory):** **Night of the Beast**
    *   *Effect:* Grants a temporary buff related to the Beast theme (often increasing damage or defense against beast-type enemies).
*   **Key Mechanics:** High mobility, fireball attacks, and the ability to split its body. The original form retains the flail sword, while clones use swords.

### **2. Adel, Baron of Night (Gaping Jaw)**
*   **Description:** A colossal black dragon with a sideways jaw and insatiable hunger. In Phase 2, it harnesses lightning powers.
*   **Primary Weakness:** **Poison Status Effect**. (It takes full upfront damage when poisoned and vomits up the contents, creating a hazard).
*   **Unique Relic Dropped (First Victory):** **Night of the Baron**
    *   *Effect:* Unlocks specific buffs or items related to the Baron's lore.
*   **Key Mechanics:** Heavy slashing attacks, biting grabs that cause Blood Loss, and summoning cyclones in Everdark mode.

### **3. Gnoster, Wisdom of Night (Sentient Pest)**
*   **Description:** A duo boss consisting of a giant white moth (Gnoster) and a scorpion-like insect (Faurtis Stoneshield). They fight separately in Phase 1 and together in Phase 2.
*   **Primary Weakness:** **Fire Damage**.
*   **Unique Relic Dropped (First Victory):** **Night of the Wise**
    *   *Effect:* Provides intelligence-based buffs or knowledge-related items.
*   **Key Mechanics:** The moth casts magic and poison spells; the scorpion stomps and burrows. Players must manage parasites if the moth infects them.

### **4. Maris, Fathom of Night (Augur)**
*   **Description:** A gelatinous, translucent entity resembling an Elden Beast but aquatic. It floats above the arena and controls bubbles/jellyfish.
*   **Primary Weakness:** **Lightning Damage**. (Lightning easily staggers it during channeling attacks).
*   **Unique Relic Dropped (First Victory):** **Night of the Fathom**
    *   *Effect:* Likely provides FP restoration or water-themed buffs.
*   **Key Mechanics:** Hypnotic sleep channels, spawning jellyfish swarms, and dropping bombs that inflict Sleep buildup.

### **5. Libra, Creature of Night (Equilibrious Beast)**
*   **Description:** A goat-headed demon obsessed with fairness who acts as a merchant before the fight, offering random "Monkey's Paw" deals (buffs/penalties).
*   **Primary Weakness:** **Madness Status Effect**. (Inflicting Madness breaks his barrier and stuns him).
*   **Unique Relic Dropped (First Victory):** **Night of the Demon**
    *   *Effect:* Unlocks Demon-themed relics or buffs.
*   **Key Mechanics:** Uses both Erdtree and Frenzied Flame incantations. He summons false gold pieces to heal players if they get Mad.

### **6. Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow (Darkdrift Knight)**
*   **Description:** A masked, one-armed centaur champion who channeled the sacred power of the Night. He regrows his left arm in Phase 2.
*   **Primary Weakness:** **Lightning Damage**.
*   **Unique Relic Dropped (First Victory):** **Night of the Champion**
    *   *Effect:* Grants combat-focused buffs or weapon affinities.
*   **Key Mechanics:** Fast, heavy-hitting melee combos. His missing arm regenerates into an amorphous dark limb in Phase 2.

### **7. Caligo, Miasma of Night (Fissure in the Fog)**
*   **Description:** A four-winged prehistoric dragon with frigid powers, reminiscent of an Everlasting Dragon.
*   **Primary Weakness:** **Fire Damage**.
*   **Unique Relic Dropped (First Victory):** **Night of the Miasma**
    *   *Effect:* Provides resistance or fire-affinity bonuses.
*   **Key Mechanics:** Ice-based attacks, summoning frost hazards, and creating fissures in the ground.

### **8. Heolstor the Nightlord (Night Aspect)**
*   **Description:** The main antagonist and final boss. A patchwork of champions formed from corpses, wielding the Moonlight Sword infused with Night power.
*   **Primary Weakness:** **Holy Damage**. (Heolstor is crippled and debuffed heavily by Holy attacks).
*   **Unique Relic Dropped (First Victory):** **Night of the Lord**
    *   *Effect:* Major narrative progression item, likely granting access to the True End or significant lore items.
*   **Key Mechanics:** Two phases (Shape of Night vs. Heolstor). He cleaves rifts in the sky to draw power from other realms, changing the skybox and affinity of his attacks.

---

### **DLC Nightlords (The Forsaken Hollows)**

#### **9. Traitorous Straghess (Dreglord)**
*   **Description:** A massive mound of flesh formed from countless discarded corpses, wielding a staff. It evolves through multiple phases, becoming more agile and summoning rot mounds.
*   **Primary Weakness:** **Holy Damage** (Though noted as having no obvious weakness, killing Putrid Corpses with Fire creates pools of fire instead of rot).
*   **Unique Relic Dropped (First Victory):** **The Night of Dregs**
    *   *Effect:* Unlocks the "Will of Balance" relic rite.
*   **Key Mechanics:** Four distinct phases, including a transformation into "Pure Impulse Straghess" with a second health bar.

#### **10. Weapon-Bequeathed Harmonia (Balancers)**
*   **Description:** Seven white-winged valkyries clad in armor resembling flowers. They purify chaos and restore balance using heroic weapons.
*   **Primary Weakness:** **Sleep Status Effect**. (Sleep causes them to fall into a deep slumber, making them vulnerable).
*   **Unique Relic Dropped (First Victory):** **The Will of the Balancers**
    *   *Effect:* Unlocks the "Will of Balance" for Collector Signboard exchange.
*   **Key Mechanics:** Synchronized diving attacks, spear waves, and transforming into a bloodflower Tree Spirit in late phases.

---

### **Summary Table**

| Nightlord | Title | Primary Weakness | Unique Relic (1st Clear) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gladius** | Beast of Night | **Holy** | Night of the Beast |
| **Adel** | Baron of Night | **Poison** | Night of the Baron |
| **Gnoster** | Wisdom of Night | **Fire** | Night of the Wise |
| **Maris** | Fathom of Night | **Lightning** | Night of the Fathom |
| **Libra** | Creature of Night | **Madness** | Night of the Demon |
| **Fulghor** | Champion of Nightglow | **Lightning** | Night of the Champion |
| **Caligo** | Miasma of Night | **Fire** | Night of the Miasma |
| **Heolstor** | Nightlord / Night Aspect | **Holy** | Night of the Lord |
| **Straghess** | Dreglord | **Holy** (Best Effort) | The Night of Dregs |
| **Harmonia** | Balancers | **Sleep** | The Will of the Balancers |

*Note: Defeating these bosses also grants **Murk**, **Runes**, and **Sovereign Sigils** (for Everdark Sovereign versions), which can be exchanged at the Collector Signboard for exclusive Relics.*

## Overview[]

Boss encounters in [Limveld](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Limveld "Limveld") are randomized at the start of each [Expedition](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Expeditions "Expeditions"). Surviving two in-game nights leads to a climactic battle against one of eight final [Nightlord bosses](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords").

## Nightlords[]

Nightlords are fought on the third night. ## Nightlord Weaknesses[]

Each Nightlord has a scripted weakness to a particular source of damage. For example, dealing even a small amount of [Lightning damage](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lightning_damage "Lightning damage") to [Maris, Fathom of Night](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Maris,_Fathom_of_Night "Maris, Fathom of Night") as it channels its global [Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") spell is enough to break its [stance](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stance "Stance") and cancel the attack. The [damage negation](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Damage_Negation "Damage Negation") and [status resistances](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Resistance "Resistance") for each Nightlord boss are listed in the table below. A **positive** value indicates reduced negation (more damage taken), while a **negative** value indicates increased damage negation (less damage taken). For [Resistances](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Resistance "Resistance"), lower values indicate a vulnerability (faster buildup), while higher values require more buildup to inflict the [Status Ailment](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Status_Effects "Status Effects"). These weaknesses still apply if the boss is fought on Day 1 or Day 2.

- [Damage Types](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Damage_Types "Damage Types")
  - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
  - A positive value (+%) indicates bonus damage.
  - A negative value (-% -% -%) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- [Resistances](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Resistances "Resistances")
  - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
  - The **🛇** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

## Everdark Sovereigns[]

[Everdark Sovereigns](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Everdark_Sovereigns "Everdark Sovereigns") are challenging versions of the standard [Expeditions](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Expeditions "Expeditions"), available for a limited time on a weekly rotation. The Everdark Sovereigns in active weekly rotation are [Tricephalos](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Tricephalos "Tricephalos"), [Gaping Jaw](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gaping_Jaw "Gaping Jaw"), [Sentient Pest](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sentient_Pest "Sentient Pest"), [Augur](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Augur "Augur"), [Equilibrious Beast](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Equilibrious_Beast "Equilibrious Beast"), [Darkdrift Knight](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Darkdrift_Knight "Darkdrift Knight"), and [Fissure in the Fog](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fissure_in_the_Fog "Fissure in the Fog"). Additional Everdark Sovereign Expeditions are scheduled to appear in future [updates](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Updates "Nightreign Updates"). This feature is not available in offline mode.

Players can only challenge an Everdark Sovereign after defeating its standard [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") form. The Nightlord **bosses** of Everdark Sovereign missions are significantly more difficult, featuring upgraded strength and new movesets. They start at Phase 2 and advance to an empowered Phase 3. Defeating an Everdark Sovereign grants [![Sovereign Sigil](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/ERN_Icon_Menu_Sovereign_Sigil.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sovereign_Sigil "Sovereign Sigil") [Sovereign Sigils](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sovereign_Sigil "Sovereign Sigil"), with a bonus for first-time victories. Sigils can be exchanged for exclusive [Relics](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Relics "Relics") and other rare items at the [Collector Signboard](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Collector_Signboard "Collector Signboard").

## Notes[]

- Bosses are promoted or simply get stronger on day two.
- Bosses do not regenerate [health](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/HP "HP") over time or between days.
- Defeating a boss creates a [Site of Grace](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sites_of_Grace "Sites of Grace") and a blue, purple, or gold [Dormant Power](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Dormant_Power "Dormant Power"). Interacting with the object opens a menu with two to three reward choices. [Nightfarers](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightfarers "Nightfarers") may obtain boss loot even if they were too far away to earn [runes](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Runes "Runes"). The object will not vanish or expire between days.
  - They can drop [Armaments](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Armaments "Nightreign Armaments"), [Smithing Stones](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Smithing_Stones "Smithing Stones"), or a passive [boon](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Effects#Dormant_Powers "Nightreign Effects") that is bound to the character for the remainder of the Expedition.
- [Evergaols](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Evergaols "Evergaols") contain bosses, but must be unlocked with a [Stonesword Key](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stonesword_Key "Stonesword Key").
- [Version 1.01](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Updates "Nightreign Updates"): the [Runebear](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Runebear "Runebear") duo boss is currently bugged on PC. Only one bear has the boss HP bar but both bears drop boss loot.[verified]

## Trivia[]

- Eight all-new Nightlord bosses were crafted for *Nightreign*.
- Many bosses first appeared in [*Dark Souls*](https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Dark_Souls "w:c:darksouls:Dark Souls"), [*Dark Souls II*](https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Dark_Souls_II "w:c:darksouls:Dark Souls II"), [*Dark Souls III*](https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Dark_Souls_III "w:c:darksouls:Dark Souls III"), and *[Elden Ring](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_(game) "Elden Ring (game)")*.
  - With the release of Forsaken Hollows, Dark Souls 2 has the least amount of returning bosses at only 2, while Dark Souls 1 and 3 got 3.

**Bosses** in **[Nightreign](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Elden_Ring_Nightreign_Wiki "Elden Ring Nightreign Wiki")** are powerful enemies that bring intense challenges throughout the game. These encounters can show up both out in the overworld and within more traditional points of interest. Some bosses are required to progress through the game, while many others are entirely optional. Every boss comes with its own unique set of attacks and gear, along with specific weaknesses and resistances to different damage types and playstyles. While some of the underlying mechanics carry over from Elden Ring, the bosses in Nightreign are deadlier overall, since they bring extra moves and new tactics into combat. On top of the challenge, players still walk away with unique rewards once a boss is successfully defeated. This page covers all the known bosses currently found in **Elden Ring Nightreign**.

s darkness falls over Limveld, the [Night's Tide](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night%27s_Tide "Night's Tide") begins creeping across the field, shrinking the space players have to move around in. Once night fully sets in, the group is pushed toward a confrontation that can't be avoided. A brutal battle follows as a number of powerful enemies converge on the player. Allies may end up falling to these enemies' devastating attacks, but that doesn't mean the fight is over. Critically injured allies can be brought back into the fight by attacking them with [Skills](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Skills "Skills") and [Weapons](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Weapons "Weapons"). They can also be rescued from a distance using tools such as bows or magic. These battles are demanding, but the message is clear: don't give up. Players are meant to draw on everything they've gathered throughout Limveld in order to survive and come out on top.

## Bosses Guide in Elden Ring Nightreign

### Elden Ring Nightreign Table of Contents

- [Nightreign Bosses: Guides](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Bosses#guide)
- [Nightrein Bosses: Complete List](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Bosses#list)

### Types of Bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign

- **Nightlords** serve as the primary bosses of Elden Ring Nightreign. Before matchmaking begins, players can select a targeted Nightlord at the [Roundtable Hold](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Roundtable_Hold "Roundtable Hold"). After the Night Boss is defeated on Day 2, players are teleported to a realm called the "Spirit Shelter," where they can purchase items to prepare for the Nightlord waiting behind a large stone door. In total, there are 8 Nightlords in Elden Ring Nightreign.
- **Night Bosses** show up at the end of every day, and which one appears depends on the specific day and expedition. As the Ring of Blue Flames closes in, the area available for exploration gradually shrinks. Once the Ring reaches its appropriate size, the Night Boss is summoned. **These bosses are non-optional and must be defeated to progress onto the next day.**
- **Evergaol Bosses** are found inside Evergaols, which can only be opened using Stonesword Keys. The later in the run a gaol is opened, the more powerful its boss tends to be.
- **Field Bosses appear** in open areas scattered across Limveld. While the same locations will always contain a boss across every expedition, the specific boss that shows up there can vary. The most dangerous Field Bosses are marked on the map with a [![formidable enemy](https://static0.fextralifeimages.com/file/eldenringnightreign/thumb/0/05/Formidable-enemy.png/25px-Formidable-enemy.png)](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/File:Formidable-enemy.png) icon right at the start of Day 2.
- **Location Bosses** can be found within points of interest that are marked on the map, like [Ruins](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Ruins "Ruins") and [Tunnels](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Tunnel_Entrance "Tunnel Entrance").
- **Remembrance Bosses** are exclusive bosses that are only encountered when players relive a Nightfarer's [Remembrance Quest](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Remembrance_Quests "Remembrance Quests"). These bosses require players to progress a Nightfarer's quest to fight them. Some are fought in the [Roundtable Hold](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Roundtable_Hold "Roundtable Hold") and some in [Limveld](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Limveld "Limveld"). Defeating Remembrance Bosses also rewards players with unique [Key Items](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Key_Items "Key Items") that are mainly used for progressing remembrance quests.
- **Shifting Earth Bosses** always appear when particular [Shifting Earth](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Shifting_Earth "Shifting Earth") maps are active, in or around the part of the map changed by the Shifting Earth. They're more likely to drop rewards that match the [affinity](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Weapon_Reward "Weapon Reward") of the current Shifting Earth.
- **Event Bosses** pop up randomly during expeditions, usually without any warning beforehand. They offer powerful, unique rewards to players who manage to defeat them, but failing the challenge can come with a curse instead.

**The bosses** found in **Nightreign** draw from a range of other FromSoftware titles, including Dark Souls, Dark Souls II, Dark Souls III, and Elden Ring. One notable difference from those other games is that dying during a boss fight in Nightreign doesn't reset your progress right away. Instead, a teammate can revive you so the fight can continue. It's only when every member of the party has been downed that the whole group gets teleported to a Respawn area.

### How to Unlock New Bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign

Players must meet the following conditions to unlock the new bosses in Nightreign's Forsaken Hollows:

- Defeated at least two Nightlords, which includes [Gladius Beast of Night](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gladius_Beast_of_Night "Gladius Beast of Night") ([Tricephalos](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Tricephalos "Tricephalos")) and one other Nightlord.
- Ensure that both new [Nightfarers](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Nightfarers_(classes) "Nightfarers (classes)"), [Scholar](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Scholar "Scholar") and [Undertaker](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Undertaker "Undertaker"), are unlocked and playable.

[![unlock bosses dlc elden ring nightreign wiki guide 400px](https://static0.fextralifeimages.com/file/eldenringnightreign/2/22/Unlock-bosses-dlc-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-400px.png)](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/File:Unlock-bosses-dlc-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-720px.png "File:Unlock-bosses-dlc-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-720px.png")

Once both of these conditions are met, players should head back to the chapel that opens up behind the [Small Jar Bazaar](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Small_Jar_Bazaar "Small Jar Bazaar") at the [Roundtable Hold](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Roundtable_Hold "Roundtable Hold"). It's also worth noting that in post-release patches, the Shifting Earth, Raid Events, and bases introduced through the Forsaken Hollows DLC will begin appearing in [Deep of Night](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Deep_of_Night "Deep of Night"), even during expeditions run in the base game.

**NOTE**: One thing to keep in mind: for this DLC-exclusive content to actually show up in Deep of Night, you'll need to be matched with three players who all own the DLC.

### Night Bosses in ER Nightreign

The Nightlords stand as the ultimate threat, waiting for players on the third day in limbo. The Nightfarers are the only warriors left who have a chance at stopping them and saving the land from total destruction.

Taking on a Nightlord is a different kind of challenge altogether, since these beings boast overwhelming attack power and toughness that surpasses anything players will have faced up to that point. Even so, there are ways to push back against this threat.

By carefully making their way through limbo, picking up more powerful tools and weapons with attributes that work well against each specific Nightlord, uncovering relics along the way, and growing sharper as a fighter through experience and observation, players can put victory against the Nightlord within reach.

The negation numbers are the % of your damage that gets blocked. For example, if a negation is 60, 40% of that damage by that type will go through and 60% will be negated. Bigger number = less damage. A negation of 100 means no damage goes through, and a negation of -100 mean the enemy takes 2x damage from that source. 0 means damage goes pretty much as is.

The resistance numbers are the buildup amount to trigger it. For example, if a resistance is 100 you must deal 100 points of the given buildup to trigger it. Note that these go down over time, and increase each time the effect procs. The values after the "/"s indicate the increased resistances after each successive proc.

# Gladius, Beast of Night | Elden Ring Wiki

**Gladius, Beast of Night**, also known as **Tricephalos**, is a [Night Lord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Night_Lord "Night Lord") [boss](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses "Nightreign Bosses") in *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*.

## Overview[]

Gladius is a massive, demonic wolf with three heads and an extra set of forelimbs. It swings around a greatsword on a long chain and launches massive fireballs. It can split its body into three one-headed, quadrupedal versions of itself, but only the original [shadow](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Shadowbound_Beast "Shadowbound Beast") retains the flail sword.[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gladius,_Beast_of_Night#cite_note-1) The form change is signaled by a howling roar.

Gladius may be challenged by selecting "**Tricephalos**" as the expedition target at the [Shrouded Roundtable Hold](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Shrouded_Roundtable_Hold "Shrouded Roundtable Hold"). It is confronted on the third day after traveling beyond the tree door at the [Spirit Shelter](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Spirit_Shelter "Spirit Shelter"). Tricephalos is the first Night Lord expedition and is unlocked by default. It deals ![Fire damage](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/3/3f/ER_Custom_Stat_Icon_Defense_Fire.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230421003945) [Fire damage](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fire "Fire") and is vulnerable to ![Holy damage](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/ER_Custom_Stat_Icon_Defense_Holy.png) [Holy damage](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Holy "Holy").

## Notes[]

- This [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") is fought on the final day of the [Tricephalos Expedition](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Tricephalos_Expedition "Tricephalos Expedition").
- This boss is vulnerable to a [Critical Attack](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Critical_Attack "Critical Attack") after its [stance](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stance "Stance") is broken.

## Trivia[]

- Internal name: **NocturnalCerberus**.
- Gladius was first revealed in the initial trailer and was the only Nightlord featured in the [network test](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Network_Test "Nightreign Network Test").
- Among the [Nightlords](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords"), Gladius is:
  - The first to be fought.
  - The last [Everdark Sovereign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Everdark_Sovereign "Everdark Sovereign") to debut.
- The name *Gladius* derives from the Latin word for "sword," referring to the short, double-edged blades used by Roman soldiers from the 3rd century BC to the 3rd century AD.
- Its design draws heavily from [Cerberus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerberus "wp:Cerberus"), the three-headed hound of [Greek mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_mythology "wp:Greek mythology") that guards the gates of the [underworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_underworld "wp:Greek underworld") to prevent the dead from leaving. This makes Gladius a fitting choice as the first Nightlord to be fought.
- In [Maliketh, the Black Blade](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Maliketh,_the_Black_Blade "Maliketh, the Black Blade")'s boss area at [Crumbling Farum Azula](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Crumbling_Farum_Azula "Crumbling Farum Azula"), there is a statue of a young girl surrounded by three [wolves](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Wolf "Wolf") below a prehistoric depiction of the [Elden Ring](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_(concept) "Elden Ring (concept)").
- Gladius' story is similar to that of the [spirits](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Spirits "Spirits") of the [Lone Wolf Ashes](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lone_Wolf_Ashes "Lone Wolf Ashes") summon.[[2]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gladius,_Beast_of_Night#cite_note-2) This item, alongside the [Spirit Calling Bell](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Spirit_Calling_Bell "Spirit Calling Bell"), were delivered to the [Tarnished](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/The_Tarnished_(Protagonist) "The Tarnished (Protagonist)") by [Ranni the Witch](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Ranni_the_Witch "Ranni the Witch"), who was entrusted to do so by [Torrent](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Torrent "Torrent")'s former master.[citation needed]
- Curiously, the Tricephalos' expedition's description compares Gladius to shadows, a term similar to the [Shadowbound Beasts](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Shadowbound_Beast "Shadowbound Beast").
- One of Everdark Gladius' attacks is the exact same used by [Heolstor the Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Heolstor_the_Nightlord "Heolstor the Nightlord"), hinting that the latter was the swordsman in Gladius' backstory.
- Gladius is reminiscent of [Sif](https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Great_Grey_Wolf_Sif "w:c:darksouls:Great Grey Wolf Sif") from the *Dark Souls* series:
  - Both are massive wolves who wield great swords for their boss fights.
  - They each have a bond with a swordsman, whose sword they utilize.
  - Their names may have ties with the word "sword", with Gladius' being of Latin origin and Sif's arguably sounding similar to saif of Arabic origin.
- Gladius might also hold ties to the [Red Wolves](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Wolf "Red Wolf"). Interestingly, Gladius is weakest to Holy, which instead deals the least damage to the red wolves.

# Adel, Baron of Night | Elden Ring Wiki

**Adel, Baron of Night**, also known as **Gaping Jaw**, is a [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") [boss](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses "Nightreign Bosses") in *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*, encountered on the third night of the [Gaping Jaw Expeditions](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gaping_Jaw_Expedition "Gaping Jaw Expedition").

## Background[]

Adel was a marvel of the natural world—immense, regal, and unrivaled atop his perch. But when the [Night's Tide](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Night%27s_Tide "Night's Tide") drenched the old island in azure rain, all life withered and perished. Starved of prey, Adel was consumed by an insatiable, ravening hunger that grew into madness.[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Adel,_Baron_of_Night#cite_note-1)

## Characteristics[]

He is a monstrous black dragon with a sideways jaw and a bottomless appetite.[[2]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Adel,_Baron_of_Night#cite_note-2) He harnesses the power of [violet-purple lightning](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lightning "Lightning") during his second phase. As an [Everdark Sovereign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Everdark_Sovereign "Everdark Sovereign"), Adel moves at light speed and whips up a massive cyclone.

Adel deals [![Standard](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/c/ce/Elden_Ring_Damage_Type_Standard.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230415214037)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Standard "Standard") [Standard damage](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Standard "Standard") on all moves during the first phase. During phases two and three, he can also deal [![Lightning](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/8/8b/Elden_Ring_Affinity_Lightning.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230415213815)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lightning "Lightning") [Lightning damage](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lightning "Lightning"). He inflicts heavy [![Blood Loss](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/6/63/Blood_Loss.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230331180605)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Blood_Loss "Blood Loss") [Blood Loss](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Blood_Loss "Blood Loss") buildup on its biting grab attack.

Adel is resistant to [![Fire](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/d/d0/Elden_Ring_Affinity_Fire.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230415213603)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fire "Fire") [Fire](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fire "Fire"), [![Lightning](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/8/8b/Elden_Ring_Affinity_Lightning.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230415213815)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lightning "Lightning") Lightning, and [![Blood Loss](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/6/63/Blood_Loss.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230331180605)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Blood_Loss "Blood Loss") Blood Loss, and fully immune to [![Madness](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/e/ee/Madness.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230331180704)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Madness "Madness") [Madness](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Madness "Madness"). He is vulnerable to [![Scarlet Rot](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/5/51/Scarlet_Rot.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/15?cb=20230331180730)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Scarlet_Rot "Scarlet Rot") [Scarlet Rot](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Scarlet_Rot "Scarlet Rot"), [![Frostbite](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Frostbite.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Frostbite "Frostbite") [Frostbite](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Frostbite "Frostbite"), and [![Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") [Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep"); however, he is particularly affected by [![Poison](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Poison.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Poison "Poison") [Poison damage](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Poison "Poison"). When the effect is procced, Adel receives the full sum of the damage-over-time upfront, and the next round of status buildup can be applied sooner than usual. However, Adel creates a [![Poison](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/0/05/Poison.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230331180712)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Poison "Poison") Poison hazard by vomiting up the contents of his stomach.

## Strategies[]

## Notes[]

- This Nightlord can be challenged after defeating [Gladius, Beast of Night](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gladius,_Beast_of_Night "Gladius, Beast of Night") for the first time. The Everdark Sovereign Gaping Jaw Expedition is unlocked by beating Adel for the first time.
- [Dark Night of the Baron](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Dark_Night_of_the_Baron "Dark Night of the Baron") is purchased from the [Collector Signboard](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Collector_Signboard "Collector Signboard") after defeating the Everdark Sovereign.
- The standard Gaping Jaw Expedition typically features [Gaping Dragon](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gaping_Dragon "Gaping Dragon") or the [Crucible Knight](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Crucible_Knight "Crucible Knight") and [Golden Hippopotamus](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Golden_Hippopotamus "Golden Hippopotamus") duo as the second Night bosses. The Everdark Sovereign Expedition has an [Ancient Dragon](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Ancient_Dragon "Ancient Dragon") (Phase 1 & 2).

## Trivia[]

- Internal name: **DragonTyranno**.
- Everdark Adel, Baron of Night was the first [Everdark Sovereign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Everdark_Sovereign "Everdark Sovereign") to debut, appearing from June 19, 2025, 09:00 UTC through June 26, 2025, 08:59 UTC. He was followed by [Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fulghor,_Champion_of_Nightglow "Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow").
- Adel is a name of European origins that means "Noble" or "Elite".

# Gnoster, Wisdom of Night | Elden Ring Wiki

The **Sentient Pest**, including **Animus, Ascendant Light**, **Gnoster, Wisdom of Night**, and **Faurtis Stoneshield**, is a [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") [boss](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses "Nightreign Bosses") in *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*.

## Background[]

## Overview[]

This [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") is two giant insects fought on the final Night of the [Sentient Pest Expedition](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sentient_Pest_Expedition "Sentient Pest Expedition"). The hardy scorpion shakes the earth when it stomps, and the white moth casts [![Magic](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Affinity_Magic.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Magic "Magic") [Magic](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Magic "Magic") and [![Poison](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/0/05/Poison.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230331180712)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Poison "Poison") [Poison](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Poison "Poison") spells. The sandy desert arena is covered in viridian leaves during the second phase, when the pests fight together as one. During the Everdark Sovereign version of the encounter, the bosses are revived after death by Animus, Ascendant Light, a red spectral moth.

If the moth grabs a player, it infects them with a parasite. If left unchecked, it develops into a worm that deals continuous damage. Allies can destroy both the worm and its larval form by attacking the infected player.

  - The shears can burrow and perform stomp attacks. It can also go inert and harden its body during the first phase.
- Phase 2: Gnoster and Faurtis fight together as one

## Notes[]

- The moth mounts the shears like [Radahn, Consort of Miquella](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Radahn,_Consort_of_Miquella "Radahn, Consort of Miquella") and calls down cascading pillars of intense [![Magic](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Affinity_Magic.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Magic "Magic") Magic damage.
- The everdark soverign version of this fight is currently bugged, as if a group defeats both Gnoster and Faurtis at the same time, Animus will either spawn out of bounds or wont appear at all.

## Trivia[]

- Internal names: **Moth** (Gnoster) & **Bouncer** (Faurtis).[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gnoster,_Wisdom_of_Night#cite_note-Zullie0-1)
- Seemingly, Gnoster is the only Nightlord whose position is shared by more than one individual.
- All of their names might have the following origins:
  - Gnoster, from Gnosis, meaning wisdom.
  - Faurtis, from Fortis, meaning fortitude.
  - Animus, meaning soul.
- Faurtis shares some visual characteristics with the "Vinegaroon", an arachnid known as "whip scorpion".[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gnoster,_Wisdom_of_Night#cite_note-Zullie0-1)
- Faurtis has an unused model where its head and claws are missing, seemingly destroyed.[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gnoster,_Wisdom_of_Night#cite_note-Zullie0-1)

# Maris, Fathom of Night | Elden Ring Wiki

**Maris, Fathom of Night**, also known as the **Augur** and the **Master of Bubbles**, is a [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlord "Nightlord") [boss](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses "Nightreign Bosses") in *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*. Maris, Fathom of Night is the Nightlord fought on the final night of the [Augur Expedition](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Augur_Expedition "Augur Expedition"). It is highly mobile, though it is quite passive and typically floats beyond the reach of melee attackers. It rams foes at great speeds and splashes bouncing waves of spirit water. Maris has hypnotic powers that lull its foes into a deep and deadly slumber. Maris deals [![Standard](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/c/ce/Elden_Ring_Damage_Type_Standard.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230415214037)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Standard "Standard") [Physical](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Physical "Physical") and [![Magic](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Affinity_Magic.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Magic "Magic") [Magic damage](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Magic "Magic"), and its attacks may inflict [![Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") [Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep"). Its weakness is [![Lightning](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/8/8b/Elden_Ring_Affinity_Lightning.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230415213815)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lightning "Lightning") [Lightning damage](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lightning "Lightning"), which easily staggers it during certain attacks.

## Characteristics[]

Maris is a gelatinous invertebrate with an otherwise featureless face that radiates a bright white light. Its elongated, blue body contains a network of constellations. It is wrapped in a transparent shroud like jellyfish’s exumbrella, lending a crustacean-like silhouette. It swims using flexible bilateral tentacles that end in green, fin-like structures. In its second phase, long dark green ribbons unfurl behind it, trailing like strands of drifting seaweed.

## Background[]

Like the [Elden Beast](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Beast "Elden Beast"), the Augur was an ancient [stellar being](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stars "Stars") that drifted through the skies. It camouflaged itself by transforming its surroundings into a vast ocean and blending with local lifeforms.[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Maris,_Fathom_of_Night#cite_note-Augur_Expedition-1) For eons, it wandered the cosmos in a dream-like trance—until it encountered the immense and lonesome [Night](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Night "Night"). For the first time, its curiosity stirred.[[2]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Maris,_Fathom_of_Night#cite_note-Night_of_the_Fathom-2)
