### Moveset[]

*Moveset*

| Attack | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Spinning Charge** | Charges forward while spinning, damaging anything in its path and nearby. |
| **Cyclone** | Spins toward the ground, generating a damaging whirlwind centered on itself. |
| **Splash** | Slams tentacles downward, splashing a bouncing wave of water. |
| **Hypnosis** | Makes a siren sound, repositions, and enters a cradle position. Lands for an extended duration to channel a devastating and unavoidable [![Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") Sleep spell that spans the entire arena. |
| **Summon Jellyfish** | Births a swarm of [Soporific Spirit Jellyfish](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Soporific_Spirit_Jellyfish "Soporific Spirit Jellyfish") that aggressively chase players and detonate, inflicting [![Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") [Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") buildup. Additonal jellyfish are created during Phase 2. |
| **Summon Plants** | Releases a non-damaging pulse, summoning stationary [Spirit Stalks](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Spirit_Stalk "Spirit Stalk") that lash at nearby players throughout the arena. |
| **Atomic Teardrop** | Drops large, luminous droplets that slowly fall from above and explode upon reaching the ground, inflicting [![Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") Sleep in a very large area. May drop up to two bombs. Phase 2 only. |

### Augur Raid[]

The **Augur** is a lesser version of this boss encountered during the Giant Bubbles raid in [Limveld](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Limveld "Limveld"). It spawns bubbles around the map. Entering one transports the player directly to the Augur. It is more passive and uses a limited moveset. Defeating **Augur** yields [![Runes](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/4/45/ER_HUD_Icon_Runes.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20231125063458)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Runes "Runes") 50,000 [runes](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Runes_(Nightreign) "Runes (Nightreign)") and grants the Unifying Fate boon, which causes the [Flask of Crimson Tears](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Flask_of_Crimson_Tears "Flask of Crimson Tears") to also restore [FP](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/FP "FP").

### Everdark Sovereign[]

1. Everdark Maris spawns in as Phase 1
  - Defeat Phase 1 and loot a legendary [Dormant Power](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Dormant_Power "Dormant Power") containing the [Nightfarers](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightfarers "Nightfarers")' starting weapon with the Storm Ruler Skill.
2. Maris respawns as Phase 3
  - Now vast, Maris floats out of reach of most attacks and no longer spawns minions; the Storm Ruler is almost required.

## Strategies[]

Maris, Fathom of Night may initiate the encounter by slamming its tentacles to produce wide, sweeping waves that bounce like [Fire Spritestones](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fire_Spritestone "Fire Spritestone"). The waves are best avoided by rolling into them, rather than backward or to the side. Depending on character height and the amplitude of the wave, dodge rolling may not even be necessary. When Maris executes a spiraling water rush, players can similarly evade by rolling into the boss as it charges forward. On occasion, Maris generates a localized cyclone; players should disengage until the vortex dissipates before resuming offense.

Maris periodically delivers swarms of jellyfish that pursue players before detonating. These can be destroyed from range or deliberately triggered near Maris to inflict damage on the boss. Maris also summons ground-based stalks from below. These plants are similar to [Spirit Eels](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Spirit_Eel "Spirit Eel"), and attack by flailing their bodies like tentacles. These can be evaded through repositioning or neutralized directly, as they are easily destroyed. They also deal damage after being destroyed.

Maris makes a siren noise, retreats and lands and curls into a suspended sphere to channel a hypnotic incantation that rapidly induces [![Sleep](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/3/37/Sleep.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230331180745)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") Sleep buildup. This move applies to the entire arena and cannot be avoided. Therefore, this move must be interrupted immediately by closing distance and applying pressure. [![Lightning](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/8/8b/Elden_Ring_Affinity_Lightning.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20230415213815)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lightning "Lightning") Lightning-based attacks are particularly effective at disrupting the channel and avoiding [![Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") Sleep accumulation.

At approximately half health, Maris enters its second phase, becoming significantly more aggressive. It summons larger swarms of explosive jellyfish, which may be countered through the same methods as before. Additionally, it releases large luminous droplets that descend from above and explode on impact, applying [![Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") Sleep buildup. These can be intercepted before contact using ranged attacks or avoided entirely by sprinting beyond the blast radius. Despite the increased intensity, most attacks remain heavily telegraphed, allowing skilled players to time evasive maneuvers and counterattacks.

## Notes[]

- The plants, jellyfish, and teardrop are coded like NPCs.
- Plants and Jellyfish defeated by the Nightfarers release bubbles that chase and damage Maris. Destroying the slow-falling bombs releases larger bubbles that deal considerably more damage.
- Maris is a [mother](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Mother "Mother") because it births the Jellyfish.
- Maris, the Master of Bubbles, may be related to the lost oracles of the [Ancient Dynasty](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Ancient_Dynasty "Ancient Dynasty") sought by [Claymen](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Clayman "Clayman").
- The teardrop does not pass through player; players can balance them on their heads, delaying their detonation.

## Trivia[]

- Internal name: **AbstractExistence**.[[3]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Maris,_Fathom_of_Night#cite_note-Zullie0-3)
- An [augur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augur "wp:Augur") was a priest that practiced augury, the interpretation of the will of the gods by studying events observed within a predetermined sacred space (*templum*). The *templum* corresponded to the heavenly space above.
- Like [Metyr, Mother of Fingers](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Metyr,_Mother_of_Fingers "Metyr, Mother of Fingers") and the [Elden Beast](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Beast "Elden Beast"), Maris, Fathom of Night is among the oldest entities in the *[Elden Ring](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_(game) "Elden Ring (game)")* universe.
- Furthermore, Maris and the Elden Beast share a few similarities:
  - Transparent skin.
  - Glowing head.
  - Aquatic traits.
  - Sound emitted.[[3]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Maris,_Fathom_of_Night#cite_note-Zullie0-3)
- Among aquatic life, Maris appears to draw more inspiration from jellyfish in particular.[[3]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Maris,_Fathom_of_Night#cite_note-Zullie0-3)
- Because of said jellyfish inspiration, and the start of its Everdark fight involving a lesser Augur, it is inferred that Maris is not a singular entity, but several offshoots of the same being.[[3]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Maris,_Fathom_of_Night#cite_note-Zullie0-3)
- Unlike the other Everdark Sovereigns, Maris' fight does not begin from the base fight's second phase.
- The Storm Ruler mechanic of Maris' Everdark fight calls back to the *Demon's Souls* series.

### Localization[]

- Its Japanese title, 夜の深海, translates into "Deep Sea of Night".

# Libra, Creature of Night | Elden Ring Wiki

**Libra, Creature of Night** (夜の魔、リブラ, *Yoru no Ma, Ribura*), also known as **Equilibrius Beast** (調律の魔物, *[Chouritsu](https://jisho.org/word/%E8%AA%BF%E5%BE%8B) no Mamono*), is a [Night Lord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Night_Lord "Night Lord") [boss](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses "Nightreign Bosses") in *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*.

## Overview[]

Libra is a capricious, goat-headed demon obsessed with equality and fairness. He disguises himself as a [Scale-Bearing Merchant](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Scale-Bearing_Merchant "Scale-Bearing Merchant") and offers a deal before the fight. He offers three deals, pulled from a randomized pool. Each deal is a Monkey's Paw wish: it provides a powerful buff, but comes at a great cost. Players may decline to bargain or simply attack Libra outright.

| **Libra's deals** | |
| --- | --- |
| *"I wish to have great strength"* | Raises ![Strength](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/f/f9/ER_Custom_Stat_Icon_Strength_%28Color%29.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20240306011507) [Strength](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Strength "Strength"), but decreases all other Attributes |
| *"I wish to have great dexterity"* | Raises ![Dexterity](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/1/1f/ER_Custom_Stat_Icon_Dexterity_%28Color%29.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20240306011453) [Dexterity](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Dexterity "Dexterity"), but decreases all other Attributes |
| *"I wish to expand my intellect"* | Raises ![Intelligence](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/b/bd/ER_Custom_Stat_Icon_Intelligence_%28Color%29.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20240306011441) [Intelligence](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Intelligence "Intelligence"), but decreases all other Attributes |
| *"I wish to have deep faith"* | Raises ![Faith](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/e/e0/ER_Custom_Stat_Icon_Faith_%28Color%29.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20240306011428) [Faith](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Faith "Faith"), but decreases all other Attributes |
| *"I wish to be in touch with the arcane"* | Raises ![Arcane](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/b/ba/ER_Custom_Stat_Icon_Arcane_%28Color%29.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20240306011416) [Arcane](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Arcane "Arcane"), but decreases all other Attributes |
| *"I want resistance to ailments"* | Increases [Resistances](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Resistances "Resistances"), but decreases [Stamina](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stamina "Stamina") |
| *"I want to hold death at bay"* | [HP](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/HP "HP") is fully restored once when critically injured, but maximum HP is reduced. |
| *"I wish for more agility"* | Raises ![Stamina](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/2/27/ER_Custom_Stat_Icon_Stamina.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/14?cb=20240328124443) Stamina, but reduces maximum HP and FP |
| *"I want a high level"* | Grants 3 levels, but drinking the Flask subtract a level |
| *"I desire a flask"* | Adds a Flask charge, but reduces maximum HP |
| *"I desire a powerful weapon"* | Grants a random purple rarity weapon, but subtracts 2 levels. |
| *"I want to gain many levels"* | Grants levels, but subtracts a Flask charge for every level gained |
| *"I wish for eventual greatness"* | Triples HP, FP, and Stamina, but halves all other Attributes |
| *"I want the power of a demon"* | Grants an Eye that shoots enemies, which builds up [![Madness](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Madness.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Madness "Madness") Madness when used |
| *"I wish to fight at full strength"* | Player and Libra receive a temporary attack and defense buff |

## Notes[]

- This [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") is fought on the final day of the [Equilibrious Beast Expedition](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Equilibrious_Beast_Expedition "Equilibrious Beast Expedition").
- This boss is vulnerable to a [Critical Attack](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Critical_Attack "Critical Attack") after its [stance](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stance "Stance") is broken.
- When Libra starts pummeling the ground and summoning a Madness aura, run around and collect as many false-gold pieces around the arena as you can. Each one heals you a bit but most importantly, alleviates Madness buildup.

## Trivia[]

- Internal name: **Baphomet**.
- His connection to dubious alchemy and counterfeit gold are likely a play on the fact that the Japanese word for western alchemy, 錬金術 (*[Renkinjutsu](https://jisho.org/word/%E9%8C%AC%E9%87%91%E8%A1%93)*, lit. the art of refining gold) refers in modern parlance to hucksters making money through unethical means and scams.
- He wields his staff in his left hand. Making him the next unique left-handed character that Fromsoft puts in their games. There’s always at least one in each installment. That is, Iron Golem in Dark Souls 1, Fume Knight and Throne Watcher in Dark Souls 2, Old Demon King and Dancer of the Boreal Valley in Dark Souls 3, Ludwig in Bloodborne, and Messmer in Elden Ring. Artorias was also rumored to be left-handed, before his arm was shattered.
- His name, Libra, is the same as a star sign in Astrology. Its unique symbol is that of a balance/scale, and its gemstone is an Opal. Its most prominent traits are that of Balance, Diplomacy, Charm, Intelligence, and Fairness.
- Libra is referred to as a *Demon* (悪魔, *[Akuma](https://jisho.org/word/%E6%82%AA%E9%AD%94)*), making him the first of his kind in the *[Elden Ring](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_(game) "Elden Ring (game)")* universe.
  - The demons of the Demon's Souls and Dark Souls universes are known as デモン (*Demon*) in the Japanese script, a simple transcription of the English word Demon, while Libra uses 悪魔 (*Akuma*), a Japanese word which refers to demons such as the buddhist [Mara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mara_(demon)) and Christian [devil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devil_in_Christianity), tying into its links to [Baphomet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baphomet#History), a medieval Christian garbling of the name of the Islamic prophet, which was later attached to Éliphas Lévi's Sabbatic Goat, an iconic depiction of a goat-headed figure which formed the basis for Libra's design.
  - Libra's title in Japanese (夜の魔) directly calls him "Demon of Night".

# Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow | Elden Ring Wiki

**Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow**, also known as the **Darkdrift Knight** and the **Night Centaur**, is a [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") [boss](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses "Nightreign Bosses") in *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*.

## Background[]

Fulghor was a gallant and pious centaur who, in ancient times, undertook an arduous quest in service of radiant [gods](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gods "Gods") that cloaked themselves in thunder.[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fulghor,_Champion_of_Nightglow#cite_note-Darkdrift_Knight-1) When his left arm was severed from behind, he realized his comrades had betrayed him and the gods they served.[[2]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fulghor,_Champion_of_Nightglow#cite_note-Night_of_the_Champion-2)

Fulghor later encountered and embraced the [Night](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Night "Night"), but his holy zeal did not falter. He channeled a sacred form of the Night's power and was consumed by battle, becoming a Nightlord and the champion of Nightglow.[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fulghor,_Champion_of_Nightglow#cite_note-Darkdrift_Knight-1)

## Overview[]

Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow is the [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") fought on the final night of the [Darkdrift Knight Expedition](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Darkdrift_Knight_Expedition "Darkdrift Knight Expedition"). The Darkdrift Knight is a masked, one-armed centaur with a massive sword. He is a swift, heavy-hitting boss with high mobility. During the second phase, he grows a new left arm.

## Drops[]

- [Night of the Champion](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Night_of_the_Champion "Night of the Champion") (first victory)
- Random [Relics](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Relics "Relics")
- [Murk](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Murk "Murk")
- [Sovereign Sigils](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sovereign_Sigil "Sovereign Sigil") (Everdark Sovereign)

## Moveset[]

- Phase 1: Missing left arm
- Phase 2: Amorphous Night left arm

### Everdark Sovereign[]

- Phase 2: Amorphous Night left arm
- Phase 3: Restored left arm; gains a bow and twinblade. Hair turns from red to gold.

## Strategies[]

## Notes[]

- This Nightlord must be defeated during [Ironeye](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Ironeye "Ironeye")'s Remembrance quest.
- Fulghor appears to be blind.

### Bugs[]

- [Update 1.01.2](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Updates "Nightreign Updates"): Defeating Fulghor will not advance the [Revenant](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Revenant "Revenant")'s remembrance quest, despite being listed as a possible choice.[verified]

## Trivia[]

- Internal name: **Centaurus**.[[3]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fulghor,_Champion_of_Nightglow#cite_note-3)
- Fulghor was the second [Everdark Sovereign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Everdark_Sovereign "Everdark Sovereign") to debut.[[4]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fulghor,_Champion_of_Nightglow#cite_note-4)
- Among the [Nightlords](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords"), Fulghor is the only one whose title is not simply just "of Night", rather "of Nightglow".
- During the Everdark fight, Fulghor's glowing cross bears some resemblance to [Miquella's Cross](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Miquella%27s_Cross "Miquella's Cross").
- Also in his Everdark form, Fulghor is able to air-walk, not unlike [Spirits](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Spirits "Spirits") such as [Torrent](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Torrent "Torrent") and the [Ancestor Spirit](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Ancestor_Spirit "Ancestor Spirit").
- Fulghor shares some characteristics with [Gundyr](https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Iudex_Gundyr "w:c:darksouls:Iudex Gundyr") from the *Dark Souls* series:
  - Their heavy build, armor, and helmet design.
  - Their transformation with an oversized, left arm of darkness.
  - Their alternate encounter, with both as their non-afflicted selves.

# Heolstor the Nightlord | Elden Ring Wiki

| ![Did you mean…?](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/f/f9/ER_Map_Icon_Guidance_of_Grace_Right.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/40?cb=20240814024206) | For the bosses, seek [Nightlords](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords").   For the title, seek [Lord of Night](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lord_of_Night "Lord of Night"). |
| --- | --- |

**Heolstor the Nightlord** (夜の王、ナメレス, *Yoru no Ō, Nameresu*, lit. Lord of Night, Nameless) also known as the **Night Aspect** (夜を象る者, *Yoru o Katadorumono*), the **Primordial Nightlord** (原初の夜の王, *Gensho no Yoru no Ō*), and **The Shape of Night** (夜の輪郭, *Yoru no Rinkaku*), is the primary [antagonist](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Characters "Nightreign Characters") and final [boss](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses "Nightreign Bosses") of *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*.

## Overview[]

This [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlord "Nightlord") has two primary phases of its fight. The initial phase is against **The Shape of Night**. A thick black miasma escapes from its body when it is slain. The [Nightfarers](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightfarers "Nightfarers") are transported to another space to fight **Heolstor the Nightlord**. Defeating the second phase triggers a special event during certain quests.

Heolstor holds a unique Moonlight Sword that wields the power of Night. He is a patchwork of champions, but his original self's undying hatred for all things is what drives him, nothing else.

## Background[]

According to its Relic, Heolstor was once a man and a knight who was beaten by some nameless hero, along with countless other warriors. The country they fought for was destroyed, and they were left in a massive mound of corpses. He was the only one whose willpower allowed him to cheat death and rise from the pile, only to curse the world forever.[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Heolstor_the_Nightlord#cite_note-1)

The Night Lord became the ruler of the [Lands Between](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lands_Between "Lands Between") after [the Shattering](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/The_Shattering "The Shattering").[verification needed] It wields the power to summon monsters and champions from other worlds,[[2]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Heolstor_the_Nightlord#cite_note-2) and is responsible for the [Night's Tide](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Night%27s_Tide "Night's Tide"). The [Nightfarers](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightfarers "Nightfarers") of the [Roundtable Hold](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Shrouded_Roundtable_Hold "Shrouded Roundtable Hold") work together to overthrow the Nightlord and save [Limveld](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Limveld "Limveld").[[3]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Heolstor_the_Nightlord#cite_note-3) Its realm is accessible by entering a petrified tree in the [Spirit Shelter](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Spirit_Shelter "Spirit Shelter") at the end of the second day.[[4]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Heolstor_the_Nightlord#cite_note-4)

## Resistances[]

- [Damage Types](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Damage_Types "Damage Types")
  - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
  - A positive value (+%) indicates bonus damage.
  - A negative value (-% -% -%) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- [Resistances](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Resistances "Resistances")
  - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
  - The **🛇** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

## Boss Fight[]

Heolstor can be fought on the Third day or the Final Day during the [Night Aspect](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Expeditions "Expeditions") expedition. Like all the other [Nightlords](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords"), its boss fight can be accessed through the [Spirit Shelter](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Spirit_Shelter "Spirit Shelter").

Its arena is the same as with all Nightlords.

### The Shape of Night[]

#### Stats[]

- ![HP](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/ER_Custom_Stat_Icon_HP.png) **4, 984** **·**; **9,968** **··**; **14,952** **∴**
- [Stance](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stance "Stance"): **130**
- It is vulnerable to [Critical Attacks](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Critical_Attack "Critical Attack") after it is [Parried](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Parrying "Parrying") or its [Stance is broken](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stance_Break "Stance Break").
- [Multiplayer](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Multiplayer "Multiplayer") is enabled.

### Heolstor the Nightlord[]

#### Stats[]

- ![HP](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/ER_Custom_Stat_Icon_HP.png) **11, 214** **·**; **22, 428** **··**; **33, 642** **∴**
- [Stance](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stance "Stance"): **130**
- It is vulnerable to [Critical Attacks](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Critical_Attack "Critical Attack") after it is [Parried](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Parrying "Parrying") or its [Stance is broken](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stance_Break "Stance Break").
- [Multiplayer](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Multiplayer "Multiplayer") is enabled.

### Moveset[]

| **Moveset List** |
| --- |
| Backstab |
| Heolstor walks forward, teleports towards its target, and perform a slow three-hit combo with its greatsword. |
| Dashing Slash |
| Heolstor winds up, then quickly dashes in a straight line while using his sword to slash. |
| Wide Slash |
| It slashes its swords horizontally, starting from the left side in a wide area in front of it. |
| Pouncing Combo |
| Pounces towards a player, slashing from side to side three consecutive times. |
| Upward Slash |
| Dashes towards a player in a straight line, then does an upward slash with its greatsword. |
| Winding Thrust |
| Winds up into a stance with its sword glowing, pounces towards the player, then impales the ground in front of it. |
| Three-Hit Combo |
| Slashes its sword towards a player three consecutive times, with the last hit being a linear thrust. |
| Cover of Darkness |
| Heolstor channels a spell, making the battlefield enveloped in darkness. Projectiles of light emerging from the ground will then rain down towards the arena randomly. |
| Reality Rift |
| Heolstor flies, channels a spell, then creates a rift in the sky. It then slams the ground with an imbued sword, creating explosive fissures that radiate all around the arena. Afterwards, small eruptions on the ground will occur all over the arena. 
Heolstor randomly chooses an element to imbue his sword with; [Fire](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fire "Fire"), [Purple Lightning](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lightning "Lightning"), [Holy](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Holy "Holy"), [Poison](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Poison "Poison"), [Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep"), [Madness](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Madness "Madness"), or [Frostbite](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Frostbite "Frostbite"). |
| Dual Slash |
| Slashes twice with its imbued swords, generating fire in a straight line. |
| Flaming Three-Hit Combo |
| Heolstor performs the **Three-Hit Combo** with its swords imbued — this time, its last hit will be a horizontal slash, generating fires that erupt from the ground. |
| Flaming Fissures |
| Extends his sword and reel backwards before performing two consecutive slashes, pauses for a second, slashes twice again, then slashes once more and flies up into the air. Heolstor charges its sword up for a few seconds and then slams down to the ground to create explosive fissures, just like the Reality Rift. This attack ends his infusion phase. 
While performing slashes, the entire arena, apart from a very small area around the boss, will be covered in small erupting explosions. There are small gaps between the eruptions, but players should stay close to the boss to avoid them. |

## Notes[]

- This [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") is fought on the final day of the [Night Aspect Expedition](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Night_Aspect_Expedition "Night Aspect Expedition").
- This boss is vulnerable to a [Critical Attack](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Critical_Attack "Critical Attack") after its [stance](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stance "Stance") is broken.
- This boss has [Parriable](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Parrying "Parrying") attacks.
- This boss is vulnerable to Holy damage, with which it gets crippled and debuffed by in both phases.
- Heolstor cleaves open rifts in the sky to draw power from other realms. Each rift reveals the skybox of a different Nightlord's arena and grants a corresponding elemental [Affinity](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Affinity "Affinity").

## Trivia[]

- Internal name: **Nameless**.
- The identity of the Nightlord was leaked early when the [Nightreign Achievements](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Achievements "Nightreign Achievements") were published.
- The Nightlord may be connected to the [Lord of Night](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lord_of_Night "Lord of Night") awaited by the [Nox](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nox "Nox") of the [Eternal Cities](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Eternal_Cities "Eternal Cities").[[5]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Heolstor_the_Nightlord#cite_note-5)
  - The [Wylder](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Wylder "Wylder") can be reborn into a new Nightlord using a Silver Tear.
- He wields what appears to be the next iteration of Fromsoftware's iconic Moonlight Greatsword. Lore clues indicate that this was his original sword, and is not a Carian blade like other Moonlight Swords in Elden Ring's lore, as it does not channel the freezing power of the Moon. It instead channels the abyssal power of Heolstor's Night.
- Heolstor's story shares some similarities with that of the [Revenger](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Revenger "Revenger") of [Castle Morne](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Castle_Morne "Castle Morne"), slayed by [Godfrey](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Godfrey "Godfrey").
  - They both lost their life to a "hero".
  - It said that "[...] from the sky poured down a great rain", matching the constant rain of the castle's location, [Weeping Peninsula](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Weeping_Peninsula "Weeping Peninsula").

### Localization[]

- His Japanese name, ナメレス or *Nameresu* (pronounced nah-may-ray-su) is a somewhat unusual transcription of the word Nameless, which would normally be written ネームレス or *Nēmuresu*; seemingly prioritizing similarity between a romaji transcription of the name to the English word over phonetic matching.
- The word Heolstor is Old English for "darkness, veil".

# Traitorous Straghess | Elden Ring Wiki

**Image needed**. Please [upload pictures](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Special:Upload "Special:Upload").

**Traitorous Straghess**, also known as the **Dreglord**, is one of the [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") [bosses](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses "Nightreign Bosses") included in the *[Elden Ring Nightreign: The Forsaken Hollows](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign:_The_Forsaken_Hollows "Elden Ring Nightreign: The Forsaken Hollows")* expansion for *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*. When its health is depleted, it gains a second health bar by transforming into **Pure Impulse Straghess**.

## Characteristics[]

 	[![ERN Render Traitorous Straghess](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/5/59/ERN_Render_Traitorous_Straghess.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20251211045633)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/5/59/ERN_Render_Traitorous_Straghess.png/revision/latest?cb=20251211045633)

Traitorous Dreglord Straghess is a large, staff-wielding humanoid boss formed from discarded corpses.[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Traitorous_Straghess#cite_note-Dreglord-1)[[2]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Traitorous_Straghess#cite_note-The_Night_of_Dregs-2) The fight opens with slow, clearly telegraphed attacks, allowing consistent windows for evasion and counterattacks. At roughly 50% health, Straghess enters its second phase. It begins using attacks and spells that inflict [![Scarlet Rot](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Scarlet_Rot.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Scarlet_Rot "Scarlet Rot") [Scarlet Rot](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Scarlet_Rot "Scarlet Rot") and control space or block movement, sharply increasing the difficulty. Straghess also summons [Putrid Corpses](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Putrid_Corpse "Putrid Corpse") and [Rotmounds](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Rotmound "Rotmound") that impede and trap the players.

Upon depletion of its health bar, **Traitorous Straghess** gains a second health bar and transforms into **Pure Impulse Straghess**, initiating the third and most demanding phase. Still applying [![Scarlet Rot](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/5/51/Scarlet_Rot.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/15?cb=20230331180730)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Scarlet_Rot "Scarlet Rot") Scarlet Rot, it becomes a markedly agile and erratic melee attacker, punishing players who overextend or fail to adjust to the faster tempo. Pure Impulse Straghess frequently disengages before re-entering with high-speed lunges and unrelenting attack combos, making sustained pressure difficult to maintain. It enters the fourth phase at approximately half health, at which point it summons pillars of flesh throughout the arena. These obstructions conceal its approach and allow it to trigger a wide explosive attack, forcing players to track its position while remaining constantly mobile.

## Encounters[]

- [Dreglord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Dreglord "Dreglord") (tutorial)
- **Traitorous Straghess** (Nightlord Phases 1 & 2)
- [Pure Impulse Straghess](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Pure_Impulse_Straghess "Pure Impulse Straghess") (Nightlord Phases 3 & 4)

## Combat Overview[]

## Resistances[]

- [Damage Types](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Damage_Types "Damage Types")
  - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
  - A positive value (+%) indicates bonus damage.
  - A negative value (-% -% -%) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- [Resistances](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Resistances "Resistances")
  - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
  - The **🛇** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

## Moveset[]

## Notes[]

- Its boss clear message is "**Calamity Overcome**".
- Although no official weakness is listed, killing the [Putrid Corpses](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Putrid_Corpse "Putrid Corpse") with fire during the "Traitorous" phase will cause them to leave behind a pool of fire rather than rot.
- The [Favor of the Rotted Woods](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Favor_of_the_Rotted_Woods "Favor of the Rotted Woods") can be helpful, but will be lost during the "Pure Impulse" phase.

## Trivia[]

- The name Straghess might be inspired by the Latin word "strages", which means "slaughter, massacre, carnage".
- Though the Dreglord is no longer affiliated to the [Night](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Night "Night"), [Heolstor the Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Heolstor_the_Nightlord "Heolstor the Nightlord") is still able to channel its [Scarlet Rot](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Scarlet_Rot "Scarlet Rot").
- Straghess' features might call back to [Nito](https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Gravelord_Nito "w:c:darksouls:Gravelord Nito") and [Manus](https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Manus,_Father_of_the_Abyss "w:c:darksouls:Manus, Father of the Abyss") from the *Dark Souls* series.

# Weapon-Bequeathed Harmonia | Elden Ring Wiki

**Image needed**. Please [upload pictures](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Special:Upload "Special:Upload").

The **Weapon-Bequeathed Harmonia**, also known as the **Balancers** and **Salvation's Standard-Bearers**, are one of the [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") [bosses](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses "Nightreign Bosses") in *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*, included in the *[Elden Ring Nightreign: The Forsaken Hollows](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign:_The_Forsaken_Hollows "Elden Ring Nightreign: The Forsaken Hollows")* expansion.

## Characteristics[]

 	[![Harmonia's render.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/0/06/ERN_Render_Harmonia.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20251211045329)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/eldenring/images/0/06/ERN_Render_Harmonia.png/revision/latest?cb=20251211045329)

Harmonia's render.

The Balancers are pallid [maidens](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Maiden "Maiden") wielding victorious weapons. Their armor resembles white flowers. Their faces are similar to [Trina](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/St._Trina "St. Trina")'s and have white clothes as wings.

However, Everdark Harmonia is drenched in blood. Their clothes are red rather than white, while the wings are very rose-like and bloody. In their final form they emerge as a giant worm-like creature drenched in blood. The worm has the corpses of balancers all over its body, with one in the middle of its face that has a spear.  

## Background[]

Young Harmonia fled into the forest to seek help when ruthless marauders terrorized her small farming [settlement](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Villages "Villages"). The village girl prayed to a [statue](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Statues "Statues") of a [guardian deity](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Guardian_Deity "Guardian Deity") with a weapon raised overhead, and was granted great power. By the end, the village was steeped in red and settled in silence. Harmonia, drenched in blood, stood with a vacant stare and a heroic weapon in her grip.[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Balancers#cite_note-The_Will_of_the_Balancers-1)

She became the Balancers, seven white-winged valkyries of the heavens, sent to purify [chaos](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Frenzied_Flame "Frenzied Flame") and restore balance to the world.[[2]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Balancers#cite_note-Balancers-2)

## Moveset[]

*Moveset*

| Attack | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Purifying Light** | Channels light through the spear, sending a linear ground wave that sprouts erupting spears. Dodge or strafe sideways to exit the line and punish recovery. |
| **Circle of Purification** | Casts an outward-expanding ring of spears. Sprint outward, then dodge toward the Balancer as the ring erupts for a safe punish. |
| **Spear Swipe** | Teleports, leaps, and performs a horizontal landing swipe. Roll toward the leap and counter once or twice. |
| **Spear Thrust** | Rushes forward with a straight thrust, sometimes twice. Side-roll and circle behind during recovery. |
| **Double Spear Swipe** | Executes two wide horizontal swipes. Roll toward the first to slip behind, or roll back to disengage. |
| **Purity of Lightning** (Phase 2) | Floats with a glowing left hand, then dives for a long-range lightning grab that impales on hit. Roll toward the dive to evade. |
| **Harmonious Smite** (Phase 2) | Sequential individual dives leaving delayed explosive trails, followed by a coordinated dive and a spear barrage from above. Sprint out of trails and dodge early to avoid explosions. |
| **Dancing Spear** (Phase 2) | Gliding multi-slash sequence followed by airborne crescent projectiles. Out-run the first flurry; roll toward incoming projectiles. |
| **Smite** (Phase 2) | Leader signals synchronized dives that leave explosive trails, followed by Purity of Lightning. Reposition early and roll through the final grab. |
| **Purifying Blast** (Phase 2) | Leader vanishes; a light ray marks an impending explosion. Sprint from the ray or roll through it to counter safely. |
| **Absolution** (Phase 2) | Teleports Balancers, kneels, and releases four expanding spear-waves while gaining attack buffs. Time forward rolls into each wave. |
| **Pouncing Combo** (Phase 2) | Purifying Light → airborne retreat → pounce and thrust-flurry with diving finisher. Side-roll the Light, widen distance, and dodge the pounce and final hit. |
| **Pulverizing Slams** (Phase 2) | Repeated empowered spear-slams, upward slash, and a final explosive fissure. Roll the opener, stay behind until the slash, then dodge the fissure. |

## Strategies[]

- The [![Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") [Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") status effect is Harmonia's greatest weakness. It is easily inflicted on the valkyries, causing them to fall into a deep slumber that lasts for an extended duration, comparable to that of [Godskins](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Godskins "Godskins"). This serves as a means to control their numbers, tipping the scales. Sleeping Balancers are also vulnerable to [Critical Attacks](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Critical_Attack "Critical Attack").
- [Parrying](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Parrying "Parrying") is a valid strategy for [Wylder](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Wylder "Wylder") against Harmonia because most of her attacks can be Parried.

## Trivia[]

- Internal names.
  - Valkyries: **AngelsDaughters**.
- Harmonia's Tree Spirit form (ID: 4641) is a modified [Ulcerated Tree Spirit](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Ulcerated_Tree_Spirit "Ulcerated Tree Spirit") (ID: 4640).
- When resurrected, the Harmonia are held up by their weapons in a manner akin to puppets.
- Harmonia is fully modeled beneath their armor. Their sleeping, cherubic faces strongly resemble [St. Trina](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/St._Trina "St. Trina")'s, whose eyelids also appear to be bruised.
- Salvation Harmonia's cranial cavity houses a dark seed surrounded by six glowing sprouts—one for each of her clones—during Phase 3. It blossoms into a magnificently red bloodflower during Phase 4, transforming Harmonia into a [Tree Spirit](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Ulcerated_Tree_Spirit "Ulcerated Tree Spirit") in full bloom.
  - [Miranda](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Miranda "Miranda") and [Malenia, Goddess of Rot](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Malenia,_Goddess_of_Rot "Malenia, Goddess of Rot") also share Harmonia's ability to duplicate and bloom.
- Harmonia's name and botanical nature tacitly imply a [Numen](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Numen "Numen") [Shaman](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Shamans "Shamans") lineage: *"The flesh of shamans was said to meld harmoniously with others."*[[3]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Balancers#cite_note-3)
- They may be connected to the [Formless Mother](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Formless_Mother "Formless Mother"), since the [Lord of Blood](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lord_of_Blood "Lord of Blood") is one of her Night 2 bosses. Her Standard-Bearer armor is identical to [Varré's Bouquet](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Varr%C3%A9%27s_Bouquet "Varré's Bouquet").
- Their screech attack uses the same sound as the [Grafted Scion](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Grafted_Scion "Grafted Scion").
- Salvation Harmonia's grand bloodflower bloom unfurls in the divine "eight around one" pattern.

### Localization[]

- In Japanese, their title is written as 英雄武器の娘たち, which roughly translates to "Daughters/Girls of Heroic Weapons". The term used for them as a group coincides with their young faces.
- In Brazilian Portuguese, their boss name is rendered **Harmonia, Arma Legada**, roughly meaning "Legacy Weapon Harmonia". Here, the title makes it seem that the name refers to the weapons and not the valkyries.
